big: Rohan has three places to lend his money: a bank deposit, a company bond and a debt fund. The advertisement for each says 'safe'. They are not safe in the same way.

lines: All three say safe and steady. How do I tell them apart?
Ask three things: Is it fixed or moving? Who stands behind it? And how fast can I get my money out?

intro: A quick comparison of how each one behaves.
rows: Fixed rate, bank insured up to ₹5 lakh, penalty to exit early
Value moves daily, no insurance, usually quick to sell
Low interest, insured up to the same limit, instant access
note: The insurance limit is ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank, covering all deposits you hold in that one bank.

title: Deposits and debt funds
stops: Bank deposits are insured up to ₹5 lakh per bank
Debt funds carry the same insurance as deposits
A debt fund's value can move every day
alt: A shield checking four statements about deposits and debt funds
caps: Deposit insurance covers up to ₹5 lakh per depositor in each bank.
Debt funds have no such insurance. Their value can fall.
The unit price moves with the bonds the fund holds.
Interest is added to your income and taxed at your slab rate.

q: Meena keeps ₹8 lakh in a single bank, in one deposit. The bank fails. How much is covered by deposit insurance?
opts: The full ₹8 lakh, since all deposits are covered without any limit
Up to ₹5 lakh, so spreading deposits across banks can protect more
Nothing, since deposit insurance covers savings accounts only
Up to ₹10 lakh, since the limit applies to each separate deposit
why: The cover has a limit. It does not protect the full amount if a depositor holds more.
The limit is ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank, so spreading across banks raises the covered total.
The cover applies to deposits of all kinds, including fixed deposits, up to the limit.
The limit is per depositor per bank, not per deposit, so extra deposits in the same bank do not add cover.

q: Rohan holds a debt fund and sees its value dip 2% in a month. What is the right reading?
opts: A mistake by the bank, which must refund the loss to every investor
A sign that deposit insurance has been withdrawn from the fund
Proof that the fund has defaulted, so he must sell at once
Normal for a debt fund, since its value moves with the bonds it holds
why: A debt fund is not a bank deposit, and no one refunds ordinary price moves.
Debt funds never had deposit insurance, so nothing was withdrawn.
A small dip is usually a price move, not a default. A default would be a separate event.
Fund values move daily with bond prices, so a small dip is part of how it works.

q: Meena earns ₹10,000 interest on a deposit and is in the 30% tax slab. What is the effect?
opts: She keeps about ₹7,000, since interest is added to income and taxed
She keeps the full ₹10,000, since deposit interest is outside tax
She keeps ₹3,000, since the tax is charged on her principal instead
She keeps ₹10,000 this year and pays the tax in the next
why: Interest is added to income and taxed at the slab, so 30% tax leaves about ₹7,000.
Interest is taxable income, so it does not go untaxed, whatever the slab.
Tax applies to the interest earned, not to the principal she deposited.
Interest is taxed in the year it is earned, so waiting a year does not change the position.

q: Rohan wants his emergency money to earn a little more. Which choice is the best?
opts: Put it in a long-term bond fund, since it pays more than a deposit
Lock it in a five-year deposit, for the highest rate available
Keep it in a savings account or very short-term option, easy to reach
Invest it in a company bond with the top interest rate in the market
why: A long-term fund can fall just when he needs the money, which defeats the purpose.
A long lock-in makes the money hard to reach, and exit usually brings a penalty.
Emergency money must be there at full value on short notice, so simple and quick wins.
A top rate usually means higher risk, which is wrong for money that must be there for sure.

pts: Bank deposits are insured up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank.
Debt funds move daily and carry no insurance.
Keep emergency money simple, safe and easy to reach.
